rows.why_long: Underdog higher 2.5 needs 56% per pick for your entry; fair view 64% (fanduel 3.5, moved to this line). Averaging 3.0 over the last 8 games, higher than 2.5 in 64% of them (raw 55%, shrunk 63%). Projects 3.1 (raw 54%, shrunk 63%).
why_points: The pick: Receptions higher 2.5 on Underdog. Each pick has to win 56% of the time for a typical entry to make money; the sportsbooks' fair view (fanduel 3.5, moved to this line) is 64%.
Other apps: PrizePicks 2.5. This is the best number for the higher side.
Game log, most recent first: 1, 4, 0, 5, 5, 4, 4, 4. Weighted average 3.0; went higher than 2.5 in 6 of 8 games (64% recency-weighted).
Trending down: last 3 games average 1.7 vs 4.4 in the games before.
How much he swings: game to game he typically moves about ±1.9, so the line is 0.3 of those swings below his average (standard deviations) — a modest gap.
PFF unit matchup, for context (in the 2023-25 test it added nothing to the projection, so it is not in the numbers): -7% on his average.
PFF: DEN plays man on 27% of coverage snaps (his opponents so far 28%); he gains 1.43 yds/route vs man and 1.83 vs zone → +0% from scheme.
PFF: DEN allows 1.34 yds/route to WRs after adjusting for the offenses it faced (league 1.59) → -12% against his usual opponents.

PFF: He runs 26% of his routes from the slot (1.51 yds/route there, 1.55 outside); DEN allows 1.32 yds/route to slot WRs and 1.44 outside (league 1.54 / 1.62, opponent-adjusted) → -9% vs his usual opponents.
Projection: we expect 3.1 catches on average; in a typical game 2.8 (a few big games pull the average up, so the typical game is what we compare with the line) — 0.3 above the line.

Keeping it honest: on their own, recent games (form) say 55% and the matchup 54%. The sportsbooks are usually close to right, and these methods have only partly beaten them (weights measured on NFL week 2), so we pull them most of the way toward the market: form 63%, matchup 63%.
Bottom line: we give it 63% to win and it needs 56%. The edge is the difference: +6.7 points; that works out to about +12¢ per $1 bet over the long run.
Risks: low line - one play can decide it.
rows.glance_head: The over looks good: we expect about 2.8 in a typical game vs the 2.5 line, and his recent games and the matchup agree.
